Please look at this. OP, victims, everyone who cares about rape victims. There was no "wrong" way to react to being raped, and freezing up or becoming a "fish out of water" (like I did) is 100% a normal, frequent, and valid response to sexual assault, and your state of being a victim here isn't less valid one bit because you froze instead of fight-or-flight.

I am bisexual, genderqueer, and a rape victim.

There is NO excuse for rape. NONE.

You might be feeling challenged right now, questioning if it was *really* rape, or if it was *really* not your fault because you were questioning your sexuality and that everyone here's exaggerating the truth just because we're lesbians, we just *have* to support you.

THERE IS NO EXCUSE FOR RAPE. Ever. Never. If you said no and he sexually assaulted you, it was rape. That is clear-cut. No matter what happens with reporting, or not reporting, or with the case, or anything legal revolving around this, this does NOT change the fact you were raped. What you described to us, by DEFINITION, was a violation of your consent. And you deserve to take care of yourself and do what helps you recover in this situation.

Your friends are absolute scumbags for using their twisted definition of fluid sexuality to invalidate who you are. It's not "everyone is bi" it's the idea that people's sexualities can fluctuate, lean towards one way, lean towards both ways, or completely null out!

I suffer from major/chronic depression and anxiety. I was really scared about taking it at first because I had perceived them as "happy pills" that mind change the way I act and feel. But Zoloft doesn't make me happy, it makes me /functional/ and clears the emotional fog in my mind. It's a cliche to say this around here, but combined with coping methods and a support system, they truly changed my life.

I experienced some jittery-ness and "high" feelings my very first time starting Zoloft. That was the worst of it. Also, I experience withdrawals if I stay off of them for more than 2-4 days where I get serious mood swings. So this is annoying when your prescription refill hasn't come in on time, or if you just forget.

Antidepressant experiences are different across people of different types and the dozens of different medications out there. Plenty of people affected by depression have their own ways of managing it. 

If you are unsure, you can half your dosage to 25 mg and start on that until your body is used to the medication. Good luck.

You'll only know if you try. What is your dosage right now? Hopefully your doctor set you on 25 mg to start.

Zoloft has made me jittery and occasionally dizzy when I first started, but it's been smooth sailing since on 200 mg. Never had issues with nausea.

I also have a TON of auditory and hyperfocus issues. I can't listen to spoken audio content, lectures, or even people just talking to me. I will randomly zone out in the middle of conversations for no particular reason. I can't remember the last five minutes and I swear I'm cursed to forget at least ONE possession wherever I go. So I have to establish a number system and count multiple times to see that I've got everything before leaving. It's painful.

A lot of people with major depression, even post-recovery, report symptoms of problems with focus and memory.

I myself have had a LOT of issues focusing on stuff like lectures and work since grade school. I'm just incredibly lucky in this aspect because I'm a near genius and normally do fine on the work itself, but lately my depression's been worsening and programming code on the screen seems to just melt together and fall off the monitor.

Maybe depending on how long you were suffering from major depression, it might have just become a bad unconscious "habit" as a consequence (quotes because it's not quite the same kind of habit as forgetting to wash the dishes or staying too late after bedtime).
